question: Do two positive illuminant spectra that are exactly metameric to a fixed synthetic observer require materially different white-balanced camera-to-observer explicit colour operators on held reflectances, proving that white-point chromaticity alone is not an identifying source-normalization observation?

primary_source.title: Illuminant-Adaptive 3D Lookup Tables for Camera Color Correction
primary_source.mechanism_used: normalized illuminant white-point descriptor conditions an explicit camera colour operator
primary_source.mechanism_not_used: paper code, data, cameras, spectra, Tucker implementation, neural weights or final-RGB prediction

fixture.operator: white-balanced camera RGB to normalized synthetic-observer XYZ 3x3 matrix fitted by development-only least squares
fixture.shared_control: one pooled 3x3 matrix fitted to both illuminants because their observer chromaticity descriptors are identical
fixture.oracle: one independently fitted 3x3 matrix per illuminant; illuminant identity is used only by this diagnostic oracle

stop_rules: Do not alter observer curves, camera sensitivities, null seed, amplitude, reflectance generator, split, operator family or thresholds after any score.
Any nonpositive illuminant, observer-white mismatch, target leakage or failed oracle-quality gate closes this exact fixture.
A pass establishes only an information-theoretic synthetic source-normalization limitation; it does not falsify C2LUT on its datasets or imply that every real illuminant metamer is material.
Do not map this result to film stock, photographic quality, a product profile or a learned final-RGB path.
claim_ceiling: Synthetic spectral-integration evidence that observer white-point chromaticity can be insufficient to identify a camera colour-correction operator; not real camera calibration, real illuminant prevalence, film/stock response or product promotion.
